tutorial.title: Working with Exception Messages
tutorial.descriptionContent: Capture exceptions and explain failed operations with useful messages.
tutorial.shortDescriptionContent: Python learners who can handle specific exception types.

lessons.title: A hidden reason
lessons.interactiveContent:
Now that we can handle different errors, let’s learn how to read the messages Python gives us when something goes wrong.

If a handler only displays Import failed. Without the reason, the order is hard to fix.

lessons.title: Capture the exception
lessons.interactiveContent:
Error handlers can access more information about an error through its exception object, including the error message.

Add as error after ValueError to capture the exception in the variable error.

Make sure to pick as, followed by error.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Error handlers can access more information about an error through its exception object, including the error message.

Use as error after the exception type to capture the invalid-conversion exception in error.

Make sure to pick ValueError, followed by as, and finally error.

lessons.title: Display the message
lessons.interactiveContent:
The captured exception's message describes why the conversion failed. We can display its content instead of adding our own message.

Pass error to print() to display that message.

Make sure to pick error, followed by print, and finally error.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The captured exception's message describes why the conversion failed. We can display its content instead of adding our own message.

Pass error to print() to display that message.

Make sure to pick int, followed by error, print, and finally error.

lessons.title: Print the details
lessons.interactiveContent:
By displaying the message carried by error, we can understand the issue the program encounters.

Make sure to pick ValueError followed by as and then error, error.
lessons.hardModeContent:
By displaying the message carried by error, we can understand the issue the program encounters.

Make sure to pick int, followed by ValueError, as, error, and finally error.

lessons.title: Store the message
lessons.interactiveContent:
print() Can print that exact message as it is a string. However, it's not of type string.

Convert error to a string and store it in message.

Make sure to pick message, followed by str(error), and finally message.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The exception object is not a string, even though print() can display its message.

Convert error to a string and store it in message.

Make sure to pick message, followed by str(error), and finally message.

Convert error to a string and store it in message.

Make sure to pick message, followed by str(error).
lessons.hardModeContent:
An exception is an object. Convert its message to a string with str().

Convert error to a string and store it in message.

Make sure to pick message, followed by str, and finally error.

lessons.title: Store the message - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Once converted to a string, we can use it as we would any other string variable.

Convert error to a string and store it in message.

Make sure to pick message, followed by str(error), and finally message.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Once converted to a string, we can use it as we would any other string variable.

Convert error to a string and store it in message.

Make sure to pick message, followed by str, +, and finally message.

lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the message carried by the captured KeyError.

lessons.interactiveContent:
Capture the ValueError in a variable named error.

Make sure to pick except, followed by ValueError, and finally as error.
lessons.hardModeContent:

Make sure to pick except, followed by ValueError, and finally as error.

lessons.title: Recall the alias
lessons.interactiveContent:
Capture the ValueError using the alias introduced in this chapter.

Make sure to type as error.

lessons.title: Add operation context
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's look at other ways to work with an exception message that explains the technical problem.

print() can display context before the details in error.

Make sure to pick print, followed by "Price failed: ", and finally + message.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Let's look at other ways to work with an exception message that explains the technical problem.

print() can display context before the details in error.

Display Price failed: followed by the stored message without requesting input.

Make sure to pick =, followed by print, "Price failed: ", and finally +.

lessons.title: Label the failed step
lessons.interactiveContent:
print() converts error to text for us, so we can print it directly.

Make sure to pick print, followed by error.
lessons.hardModeContent:
print() converts error to text for us, so we can print it directly.

lessons.title: Label the failed step - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we use print() with multiple arguments, we can combine a string and the error without converting the error message to a string first.

Add Price failed: before the exception details to identify the failed conversion.

Make sure to pick "Price failed:", followed by ,, and finally error.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If we use print() with multiple arguments, we can combine a string and the error without converting the error message to a string first.

Add Price failed: before the exception details to identify the failed conversion.

Make sure to pick "Price failed:", followed by ,, and finally error.

lessons.title: Build one message
lessons.interactiveContent:
An f-string can combine operation context and exception details into one value.

Place error inside the f-string to include its message.

Make sure to pick f followed by { and then error, }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
An f-string can combine operation context and exception details into one value.

Place error inside the f-string to include its message.

Store a message beginning with Price failed: , followed by the exception details, and print it.

Make sure to pick ValueError, followed by f, {error}, and finally message.
